heroText: Odense is Funen's main city and the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen, with museums, parks and an easy-going university-town centre. Begin at Hans Christian Andersen House, add Brandts for art and culture, then use Munke Mose or the Funen Village for a slower afternoon. Most arrivals come by train or through Copenhagen, Billund or nearby Hans Christian Andersen Airport.

areas.name: Odense city centre
areas.text: The centre is best for first stays, with Andersen sights, restaurants, shops and the station close together.

areas.name: Brandts area
areas.text: The Brandts area has culture venues, cafes and nightlife on the western side of the central core.

areas.name: Munke Mose
areas.text: Munke Mose is a green riverside base for quieter walks, families and easy access back into town.

areas.name: Skibhuskvarteret
areas.text: Skibhuskvarteret offers local streets, apartment stays and good access north of the station.

airports.name: Hans Christian Andersen Airport (ODE)
airports.search: Hans Christian Andersen Airport, Odense, Denmark
airports.text: Hans Christian Andersen Airport is north of Odense and mainly useful for limited services and private aviation.

airports.name: Billund Airport (BLL)
airports.text: Billund Airport often has more international routes for Odense visitors using road or rail connections across Jutland and Funen.

airportTransfer.value: 15-25 min from Hans Christian Andersen Airport, longer from Billund or Copenhagen
airportTransfer.distance: about 12 km north of central Odense

stayOverview: Odense city centre is the easiest base for Andersen sights and restaurants, Brandts suits culture-led stays, Munke Mose is calmer and greener, and Skibhuskvarteret works for apartments and longer visits.
hotelIntro: Odense is compact and rail-friendly. Central hotels keep the museums simple, Brandts adds nightlife and culture, Munke Mose suits slower family stays, and Skibhuskvarteret gives a more residential base.
rentalCars: You do not need a car in Odense, but one helps for Funen villages, castles and coastal detours.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in the city centre if Hans Christian Andersen House and restaurant walks are the main plan.

travelTips.title: Arrival
travelTips.text: Odense is often easiest by train, so compare rail routes before choosing a distant airport transfer.

travelTips.title: Museums
travelTips.text: Keep one indoor culture stop in the Odense plan so rain, heat or short winter daylight do not break the day.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Egeskov Castle is the classic Funen outing, best with a car or carefully planned public transport.

history.label: c. 2000 BCE
history.text: Archaeological excavations in the vicinity show proof of settlement for over 4,000 years since at least the Stone Age.
The territory, previously part of the vast Archbishopric of Hamburg, was created a Catholic diocese in 988.

history.label: 12th century
history.text: The first church in Odense appears to have been St Mary's, probably built in the late 12th century.

history.label: 13th century
history.text: In 1720, Frederick IV ordered the rebuilding of Odense Palace, partly on the foundations of the 13th century St.
Greyfriars Monastery (Gråbrødre Kloster) was founded by the Franciscans in 1279.

history.label: 18th century
history.text: Glove production, which had begun in the 18th century, developed into one of the most important industries while the harbour facilities were further expanded.
An 8 kilometre (5.0 mi) long, 7.5 metre (25 ft) deep canal from Odense Harbour to Odense Fjord was built between 1796 and 1806 to facilitate the growth of Odense as a port city.
In 1853 Denmark's first modern water and gas works were opened in Odense.
Commerce was further boosted by the building of a railway across Funen in 1865, and Odense became one of Denmark's largest rail junctions.
Odense Central Library was established in 1924 and removed to Odense station in 1995.
Odinstårnet was blown up by a Danish Nazi group in 1944 and has never been rebuilt.

history.label: 1960s
history.text: From the 1960s Odense increasingly became a cultural hub, with the establishment of a university in 1966 and the launching of trade shows, including the large Odense Congress Centre.
In 1988 a major national television network, TV2, was established in Odense.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The Vikings built numerous fortifications along the river banks to defend it against invaders coming in from the coast.
